data.title: Balance Scale Meanings
data.description: You will answer out loud to explain what the equal sign means.

items.conceptStatement: The equal sign means both sides are the same.
items.ask: Three plus two equals five. What does the equal sign tell us about the two sides?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any words that mean the two sides match or are even count as correct.
items.signatureError: Saying the sum, five, is NOT an explanation of the equal sign.
items.correctionBody: The equal sign means both sides are the same. Here, three plus two is the same as five.

items.conceptStatement: The equal sign means both sides are the same.
items.ask: Four equals two plus two. What does the equal sign mean in this picture?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any words that mean the two sides match or are even count as correct.
items.signatureError: Saying that the answer comes next is NOT correct.
items.correctionBody: The equal sign means both sides are the same. Four is the same as two plus two.

items.conceptStatement: The equal sign means both sides are the same.
items.ask: Six equals six. What does the equal sign tell us about these numbers?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any words that mean the two sides match or are even count as correct.
items.signatureError: Just repeating the number six is NOT an explanation.
items.correctionBody: The equal sign means both sides are the same. Six is the same as six.

items.conceptStatement: The equal sign means both sides are the same.
items.ask: One plus four equals five. What does the equal sign show us on the balance scale?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any words that mean the two sides match or are even count as correct.
items.signatureError: Saying the sum, five, is NOT an explanation of the equal sign.
items.correctionBody: The equal sign means both sides are the same. One plus four holds the same weight as five.

data.title: Balance Scales and the Equal Sign
data.description: You will answer out loud to explain what the equal sign means.

items.conceptStatement: The equal sign means both sides are the same.
items.ask: Four plus one equals five. What does the equal sign tell us about the two sides?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any words that clearly state the two sides match, are even, or are identical count as correct.
items.signatureError: Saying the sum, five, is NOT an explanation of the equal sign.
items.correctionBody: The equal sign means both sides are the same. Four plus one is the exact same amount as five.

items.conceptStatement: The equal sign means both sides are the same.
items.ask: Three equals three. Why can we put an equal sign right between them?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any words explaining that the amounts match or are equal count.
items.signatureError: Saying three again is NOT an explanation of the equal sign.
items.correctionBody: The equal sign means both sides are the same. Three is balanced with three.

items.conceptStatement: The equal sign means both sides are the same.
items.ask: Two plus two equals four. What is the meaning of the equal sign in the middle?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any phrasing showing that the left side and right side weigh the same or are equal counts.
items.signatureError: Saying that the answer comes next is NOT correct.
items.correctionBody: The equal sign means both sides are the same. Two plus two is balanced with four.

items.conceptStatement: The equal sign means both sides are the same.
items.ask: Six equals five plus one. What does the equal sign show about these two parts?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any words stating that both sides match or are balanced count.
items.signatureError: Saying the sum, six, is NOT an explanation of the equal sign.
items.correctionBody: The equal sign means both sides are the same. Six is the exact same amount as five plus one.

input.objectiveText: Explain the secret rule behind a repeating or growing pattern
input.intent: Have the tutor show a simple pattern (such as 2, 4, 6, 8 or red-blue-red-blue) and let students say the rule aloud into the microphone (e.g., 'plus two' or 'red then blue').

data.title: Pattern Rules
data.description: Listen to the patterns and say the rules out loud.

items.conceptStatement: This pattern alternates between big and small sizes.
items.ask: Big, small, big, small. What is the rule of this pattern?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Any phrasing describing the alternating big and small sizes counts as the answer.
items.signatureError: Saying the next word, big, is NOT the rule.
items.correctionBody: The rule is big then small because the sizes alternate back and forth.

items.conceptStatement: This pattern grows by adding five each time.
items.ask: Five, ten, fifteen, twenty. What is the growing rule here?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Counting by fives or saying add five counts as the answer.
items.signatureError: Saying the next number, twenty-five, is NOT the rule.
items.correctionBody: Each number goes up by five every time. The rule is plus five.

items.conceptStatement: This pattern grows by adding three each time.
items.ask: Three, six, nine, twelve. What is the growing rule of this pattern?
items.howToPlay: I will show you something, and you tell me what it means in your own words.
items.acceptRule: Saying add three or counting by threes counts as the answer.
items.signatureError: Saying the final number, twelve, is NOT the rule.
items.correctionBody: The numbers grow by adding three each step. The rule is plus three.
